summary: Anjali’s employee and Jira account identifiers persist through the July 2025 surname and email change. She makes independent product trade-offs and has stronger research capability than the exported snippets demonstrate; a technical appendix on a page she created was written by an engineer.
archetype: Product manager with identity continuity and shared documents

skills.why: Observed user behaviour causes a real pilot scope change followed by a return-session check.
Maintains priorities and revises commitments based on adoption and dependencies.
Resolves a commercial request against operator needs with an agreed temporary arrangement.
Removes acceptance ownership blockers and tracks the resulting improvement across iterations.
Support validation establishes that her rollout instructions are usable.

Private recordings and research notes show independent study planning and synthesis. Exported work shows designer review and partial results only; hold a confident independent-research claim until those materials are available.
Can adjust a query with analyst review; training alone would not establish production analysis.
She approved acceptance wording, not the engineer’s lease or consistency mechanism.
Reporting the retry failure did not involve implementing or reviewing Go code.
Commenting on linked designs is not the ability to build components or prototypes.

decoys.why: Page creation metadata conceals the engineering authorship split unless revision notes are considered.
Reporter attribution alone does not convey implementation skill.
A design viewer is not a practitioner of the tool.

traps.plant: The HCM change event ties both surnames and email intervals to one Jira account and employee key; the older PRD retains its original author name.
The PM-created addendum credits most technical content to recon-maintainer-kc and limits product approval to behaviour.
A completed SQL course sits beside a ticket showing analyst correction; completion must not imply independent querying.

answer_behavior.notes: Confirms product work; redirects backend design questions to engineering. Research confirmation can succeed despite insufficient exported proof.
